concepts.def: Ratio of observable traits among offspring
Both alleles expressed equally in a heterozygote
Gene on the X chromosome (e.g. colour-blindness)
Family tree showing inheritance through generations

walkthroughs.body_html:
Bb × bb gives a 1 : 1 ratio.

Punnett: Bb, Bb, bb, bb. Half the offspring show the dominant trait, half the recessive.

Alleles I^A and I^B are codominant; i is recessive. Genotype I^A I^B → blood group AB.

Cross I^A i × I^B i → I^A I^B, I^A i, I^B i, ii → AB, A, B, O.

Colour-blindness allele is on X and recessive. Females need two copies to be affected; males need only one.

X^B X^b × X^B Y → 25% chance of an affected son.
